properties.name: OH-75 parkway (Broerman to Ludlow)
properties.section: 40.2 m: planted median 4.0, BRT 3.5 + 0.5 separator each way, two 3.5 m lanes each way with 0.6 and 1.5 m shoulders, 2.5 m verge and 2.5 m walk
properties.note: Storrow/Jamaicaway parkway (highway map): compact ramps at the major crossings, signals at minor streets, local trucks only. At km 18.96, on Albone Street's axis, a continuous T with Central Parkway (Ben, 22 October: square with Albone and angled to OH-75, about 66 degrees): southbound through never stops; two protected left lanes into Central Parkway sit in the median, widened to 7.5 m for 100 m before the T (left-turners cross the southbound bus lane before the junction, so the southbound BRT runs straight through with the general lanes); northbound through and the northbound BRT stop for that phase; Central Parkway turns right from both lanes onto northbound OH-75, the outer lane becoming a third northbound lane in the shoulder and verge that drops north-east of the T (where is not set). Banned: Central Parkway to Millvale Boulevard south-west, and the northbound right into Central Parkway (those use Ludlow, Colerain or Spring Grove). The angle is why the two banned movements go: both would be turns of about 114 degrees. Signalled junction with Ludlow at km 19.4, coordinated with the T about 438 m away

properties.name: CPW T: southbound left into Central Parkway (Phase A)

properties.text: third northbound lane drops (where not set)

properties.name: Central Parkway (to OH-75)
properties.section: 24.4 m (Ben, 23 October: Central Parkway's 80 ft): a 3.5 m kerbside bus lane, two 3.3 m lanes and a 2.1 m walk each way, no median
properties.note: Central Parkway carried on north of Ludlow to a continuous T on OH-75 at km 18.96, tangent at both ends (Ben, 22 October): it carries straight on from Central Parkway's own line (bearing 24 degrees) for 83 m, turns 22 degrees on a 1000 m curve (380 m), and runs its last 47 m on Albone Street's axis, so it lines up with Albone across the parkway and meets OH-75 at about 65 degrees. About 510 m from Central Parkway's end. The hill between Millvale, Ludlow and Central Parkway is regraded for it: the road runs nearly level (about 168 m at Ludlow to 165 m at OH-75), so the hill is cut down by up to about 32 m (LiDAR), more than 5 m over about 420 m. Kerbside bus lanes both ways (Ben: bus lanes, not necessarily BRT): northbound buses run in the bus lane straight into the right turn onto OH-75; southbound buses from the OH-75 BRT come over in the left-turn phase. Two general lanes in from the southbound left, two out turning right onto northbound OH-75. At Ludlow: no left turns from Central Parkway either way (two-phase signal); Clifton-bound traffic stays on Millvale and turns at the Ludlow signal

properties.name: Central Parkway / Ludlow (two phases, no lefts from Central Parkway)
Central Parkway (Ludlow to Reading Road)
properties.section: 24.4 m (Ben's width, 80 ft): a 3.5 m kerbside bus lane, two 3.3 m lanes and a 2.1 m walk each way, no median (as the real Central Parkway has none). 45.72 m (150 ft) at the south end and on East Central Parkway to Reading Road: 3.0 m median, centre bus lanes 3.5 m, two 3.3 m lanes, 2.5 m parking, 2.0 m tree strip and a 6.76 m sidewalk each way
properties.note: Bus lanes the whole way from Millvale (OH-75) to Reading Road (Ben, 22 and 23 October: bus lanes, not necessarily BRT), on Ben's line and widths. On the 80 ft parkway they run at the kerb; on the 150 ft end (1,714 m, from the turn south near Liberty to Reading Road) they move to the centre, beside a 3.0 m median that can carry the stop platforms, with parking and tree-lined wide sidewalks at the sides. The buses cross between kerb and centre at the change of width (signal priority there not drawn)

properties.name: OH-75: Millvale Boulevard (Ludlow to the tunnel)
properties.section: 45.72 m (150 ft, the page street): 2.0 m planted centre between the bus lanes, BRT 3.5, platform or planted strip 3.0, two 3.3 m lanes, 2.5 m loading lane, 6.26 m walk each way; one-way arms of 75 ft round the confluence park
properties.note: Drawn on the page's Millvale Boulevard streets (Ben's KMLs), not the highway map's lanes, which did not follow them closely. Signals at every crossing street (highway map). Passes under the north trunk viaduct and RER B (km 19.6), the APEx Indianapolis + RER D deck (km 20.37, R5 below it) and the RER A trunk (km 21.31, 44 degrees, about 7.6 m down in the tunnel approach cut: piers in the centre BRT strip are the natural choice)

properties.name: OH-75: English Woods tunnel
properties.section: two bores 12 m apart: each 0.6 m walls, BRT 3.5 + 0.5, two 3.5 m lanes, 0.5 and 1.0 m shoulders
properties.note: Hazardous loads use the other ring (highway map). Metro Line 9 crosses over it at km 21.53 (ground 177 m, road about 147 m, roof about 154 m): its level is not set, so it has to pass above about 157 m or below about 140 m there; North Fairmount station is about 230 m away

properties.name: OH-74 (boulevard, to Colerain)
properties.note: OH-74 ends at a signal on Colerain at Kirby. Through traffic goes down Colerain to Millvale Boulevard (path A, widened to 26.2 m); the BRT goes on along Colerain to Blue Rock, Blue Rock and Spring Grove to the Colerain stop on Millvale Boulevard. RER-1b crosses over it about 170 m short of Colerain and stays on viaduct (rail 160 m or more, road 153.5 m). West of the page OH-74 carries APEx in the centre and the RER D pair beside it in a 29.7 m median (section 73.42 m)

properties.name: Inner Ring North (OH-562 boulevard)
properties.section: 45.72 m: from the centre a 1.0 m planted centre, 3.5 m bus lane, 3.0 m platform or planted strip, two 3.3 m lanes, 2.5 m loading lane, 6.26 m walk each way
properties.note: OH-562 from Duck Creek (I-71, J8) west through Norwood to Broerman (OH-75, J7), highway map line. Pushed north (up to 46 m) between Norwood Central frame s 3330 and 4660, where the map line lay on the rail corridor west of the station and clipped its Transvalley tracks: its south edge now stays 3 m outside the six-track corridor and the station track area. Grade separations: the Waynesville pair (CL&N prong) just north-east of Norwood Central, the APEx Transcontinental at Ridge (km 2.13 from Duck Creek) and near Broerman (km 8.08); Metro Lines 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 12 and 14 pass under it in tunnel

properties.note: OH-74's through traffic and its BRT share this stretch (Ben, 22 October: path A for traffic, BRT on Blue Rock)
